text.div:
SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD

  • Work-up between episodes: blood count, metabolic and liver panels, lipase, urinalysis, TSH, morning cortisol, celiac serology, a baseline ECG, CT enterography, and upper endoscopy
  • Gastroenterology consultation to confirm the diagnosis and advise on prophylaxis, abortive treatment, and an emergency plan
  • Symptom diary: date, prodrome, length and severity of each episode, triggers, medicines taken, and emergency visits
  • Amitriptyline prophylaxis at bedtime: 25 mg, raised by 25 mg every two weeks to 75 mg (about 1 mg/kg), with an ECG at baseline, at about 50 mg, and at the target dose; judge the response after three months at target and continue for at least a year if it helps
  • Abortive plan at the first sign of the prodrome: sumatriptan 20 mg nasal spray with ondansetron 8 mg dissolving tablet, a dark quiet room, and small sips of fluid; an individualized emergency department letter for episodes that do not settle
  • Trigger management: regular meals and sleep, planning around travel and social events, early treatment of infections, and continued avoidance of cannabis
  • Anxiety and mood: GAD-7 and PHQ-9 at the first visit and every three months; relaxation breathing, with cognitive behavioral therapy offered if symptoms persist

resource.title: Charles Darwin synthetic care plan
resource.description: Evaluation and first six months of care of recurrent stereotyped vomiting episodes in a 40-year-old man: a symptom diary, the Rome IV criteria for cyclic vomiting syndrome and its red flags, a cannabis and substance history (to exclude cannabinoid hyperemesis syndrome), a work-up between episodes to exclude other causes (blood count, metabolic and liver panels, lipase, urinalysis, TSH, morning cortisol, celiac serology, CT enterography, and upper endoscopy), a baseline ECG, and anxiety and mood screens (GAD-7, PHQ-9). Management follows the 1842 ANMS and Cyclic Vomiting Syndrome Association guideline: amitriptyline prophylaxis titrated to about 1 mg/kg with ECG checks of the QTc, an abortive plan of nasal sumatriptan and ondansetron at the prodrome, an individualized emergency department protocol, trigger management, and relaxation training. The diagnosis stays provisional because it is clinical, and none of the historical theories of his illness is treated as confirmed.
